question: Xi Jinping out before 2027?
description:
This market will resolve to "Yes" if China's General Secretary of the Communist Party, Xi Jinping, is removed from power for any length of time between July 3, 2025, and December 31, 2026, 11:59 PM ET. Otherwise, this market will resolve to "No".

CCP General Secretary Xi Jinping will be considered removed from power if he announces his resignation from his role as General Secretary, or is otherwise dismissed, detained, disqualified, or otherwise loses his position or is prevented from fulfilling his duties as General Secretary within this market's timeframe.

The primary resolution source for this market will be a consensus of credible reporting.

eventMetadata.context_description: Xi Jinping's continued hold on power through 2026 reflects his extensive consolidation of authority within the Chinese Communist Party, including repeated military leadership purges that have removed potential rivals while installing loyalists. With no designated successor and the 21st Party Congress in 2027 widely viewed as the venue for a fourth term rather than a transition, elite dynamics show minimal internal contestation. Recent diplomatic engagements, including summits with foreign leaders, further signal stable governance. Traders assign over 95 percent probability to his retention because structural barriers such as party norms, surveillance mechanisms, and lack of organized opposition make abrupt removal improbable before the end of 2026. Even so, unforeseen developments like a severe health crisis or sudden elite fracture could still alter the trajectory within the resolution window.
